item.content:encoded: A versatile tool for managing coding projects, integrating multiple terminals and AI agents within a single control panel.

item.title: Brighter Than White
item.content:encoded: If you’ve got an HDR display, and use Chrome 137+ or Safari 26+ (even on iOS), perhaps you’ve seen images sometimes with colors that are so bright they seem to dim the rest of the screen. I find it a bit distracting, but I can see how it could be a fun technological gimick sometimes. […]

item.title: Dark Mode Very Much Matters To Me
item.content:encoded: It's not just vibes, it's an accessibility thing.

item.title: Custom Glow Rings Inside of Elements
item.content:encoded: A box-shadow is an obvious choice for an inner glow of an element to highlight it. But with some fancy masking, we can use any overlay style we want.

item.title: Better Centering with CSS text-box
item.content:encoded: Jake has a very nice, clear video about what text-box solves in CSS. It essentially makes even padding on an element (like a button) doable without magic numbers, and that will work across any font (sick). Temani made a tool to help pick the right values.

item.title: Extracting Grid Information Using CSS
item.content:encoded: It's an interesting and potentially useful trick to have an element know where it is on a grid. That's tricky enough when the items are in one row/column, but what about when they span?

item.title: Code Snacks
item.content:encoded: Love these little animations (“code snacks”) from Lauren Basser that illustrate basic technological concepts. Check out the ones for Working Directory and Shadow DOM — not the easiest concepts to illustrate as simply as this!

item.title: Comparing Values With CSS progress()
item.content:encoded: The new CSS progress() function maps a given value to a range. Super useful for responsive layouts, responsive typography, and fun tricks.

item.title: It’s All About The Permissions Recovery
item.content:encoded: Users who deny permissions can recover them by adjusting settings, although many may not realize this.

item.title: A Deep Dive into StyleX
item.content:encoded: StyleX has been around for a while, but it’s seeing a resurgence in popularity lately for whatever reason. Seems pretty good to me.
